passages.text: Before the year that the chief commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it, the LORD had already spoken through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and the sandals from your feet.” And Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot.
passages.sermon:
Sargon was the king of Assyria.
He sent his chief commander to Ashdod.
The commander attacked Ashdod.
He captured the city.
Before this happened, the LORD spoke.
The LORD spoke through Isaiah, son of Amoz.
The LORD gave Isaiah a command.
He said, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist.
Take the sandals off your feet.”
Isaiah obeyed the LORD.
Isaiah walked around naked and barefoot.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת בֹּ֤א תַרְתָּן֙ אַשְׁדּ֔וֹדָה בִּשְׁלֹ֣ח אֹת֔וֹ סַֽרְג֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם בְּאַשְׁדּ֖וֹד וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ אָמוֹץ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ לֵ֗ךְ וּפִתַּחְתָּ֤ הַשַּׂק֙ מֵעַ֣ל מָתְנֶ֔יךָ וְנַעַלְךָ֥ תַחֲלֹ֖ץ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֑יךָ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ כֵּ֔ן הָלֹ֖ךְ עָר֥וֹם וְיָחֵֽף׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said, “Just as My servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and omen against Egypt and Cush, so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old alike, naked and barefoot, with bared buttocks—to Egypt’s shame.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD said this about Isaiah.
Isaiah was the LORD’s servant.
Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years.
Isaiah did this as a sign and a warning.
This sign was against Egypt and Cush.
The LORD said the king of Assyria will act in the same way.
The king of Assyria will take captives from Egypt.
He will take exiles from Cush.
He will lead away both young and old people.
They will be naked and barefoot.
Their buttocks will be uncovered.
This will bring shame to Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלַ֛ךְ עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ עָר֣וֹם וְיָחֵ֑ף שָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ א֣וֹת וּמוֹפֵ֔ת עַל־ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַל־ כּֽוּשׁ׃ כֵּ֣ן יִנְהַ֣ג מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַ֠שּׁוּר אֶת־ שְׁבִ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם וְאֶת־ גָּל֥וּת כּ֛וּשׁ נְעָרִ֥ים וּזְקֵנִ֖ים עָר֣וֹם וְיָחֵ֑ף וַחֲשׂוּפַ֥י שֵׁ֖ת עֶרְוַ֥ת מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.
passages.sermon:
Some people trusted in Cush.
They looked to Cush for hope.
Some people were proud of Egypt.
They boasted about Egypt.
These people will feel dismayed.
They will feel ashamed.
passages.original: וְחַתּ֖וּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ מִכּוּשׁ֙ מַבָּטָ֔ם וּמִן־ מִצְרַ֖יִם תִּפְאַרְתָּֽם׃

passages.text: And on that day the dwellers of this coastland will say, ‘See what has happened to our source of hope, those to whom we fled for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?’ ”
passages.sermon:
The people who live on this coastland will speak on that day.
They will say, “Look at what has happened to those we trusted.
We ran to them for help.
We hoped they would save us from the king of Assyria.
Now they have fallen.
How can we escape?”
passages.original: וְ֠אָמַר יֹשֵׁ֨ב הָאִ֣י הַזֶּה֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ הִנֵּה־ כֹ֣ה מַבָּטֵ֗נוּ אֲשֶׁר־ נַ֤סְנוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה לְהִ֨נָּצֵ֔ל מִפְּנֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֵ֖יךְ נִמָּלֵ֥ט אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃ס
